summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a history of gastrointestinal bleeding was admitted with acute chest pain and melena. He had a 5-point drop in hematocrit since his recent discharge, where he had been advised to start aspirin. The anemia led to demand ischemia, causing chest pain. He was hemodynamically stable and received two units of packed red blood cells, which improved his hemoglobin. A chest X-ray showed interstitial edema, and he underwent hemodialysis. Upper endoscopy revealed nodular gastritis and an inflammatory polyp, while colonoscopy identified a non-bleeding ulcer in the hepatic flexure; biopsies were taken. Aspirin was discontinued due to GI bleeding risk. Cardiology attributed the chest pain to microvascular ischemia and recommended isosorbide mononitrate and atorvastatin instead. The patient was discharged home with stable vital signs, resolved melena, and plans for outpatient follow-up on biopsy results and pancreatic MRI. He was advised to monitor daily weight and avoid illicit substances.
